title: Attempt 1: balance → step → walk → walk fast
note: Stage rewards as first designed (see the stage table). Stopped Wed 10:36 in stage 2: tapping in a split stance (0 front-foot changes for 200+ generations).

stages.name: Balance
stages.reward: 100 × (steps survived ÷ 500) − 100 × fell − 50 × average |body tilt| − 0.5 × effort
terms: for staying up the whole episode
average |hull angle| in radians: keep the body level
effort = 0.028 × |motor command| per joint per step, summed
stages.episode: 500 steps (10 s), no early stop: standing still is allowed
stages.pass: 0 falls on 20 held-out tracks and average |tilt| < 0.15 rad
stages.expect: Stands upright on any track, body level, using little motor effort. Maximum score ≈ 100.
stages.risk: Locks into a stiff split stance (one foot forward). Harmless here, since stage 2 has to break it anyway.

stages.name: Step
stages.reward: 100 × survival − 100 × fell + 3 × front-foot changes (max 40) + alternating touchdowns (max 60) − 30 × |average foot offset| − 0.5 × effort
terms: the foot in front changes (lower legs pass each other by > 0.15), up to 40 changes = 120
a foot touches down after the OTHER foot did (left, right, left…), up to 60
average distance foot 1 is ahead of foot 2: keeps the feet centred, no permanent lead
stages.episode: 600 steps (12 s), no early stop: stepping in place is fine, moving forward is neither paid nor punished
stages.pass: ≤ 1 fall in 20, ≥ 12 front-foot changes per episode, |average offset| < 0.5
stages.expect: Marches in place or creeps forward, legs swinging past each other in turn, left-right-left touchdowns, without falling. Maximum ≈ 100 + 120 + 60 = 280.
stages.risk: Shuffles the feet back and forth while sliding them, so the front-foot changes count without real steps. The alternating-touchdown term is there to require lifting.

stages.name: Walk
stages.reward: environment reward (fall costs 20 instead of 100) − (40 × lopsided + 20 × |average offset|) × share of the course covered
terms: the environment's motor cost, per unit per step
for a fall (the real game charges 100; training uses 20 so trying steps isn't too costly)
lopsided = |2 × (share of leading time foot 2 leads) − 1|: 0 if the feet take turns, 1 if one always leads
how far one foot sits ahead on average
the gait tax grows with distance: standing pays nothing, a full-length skip pays ≈ 77
stages.episode: full 1600 steps; early stop if the body moves < 1 unit in 150 steps
stages.pass: average x ≥ 60, ≤ 4 falls in 20, lopsided ≤ 0.3
stages.expect: Turns the march into forward walking: alternating steps that carry the body most of the way along the course.
stages.risk: Drifts back to the skip (one leg as a prop), or stumbles forward and falls, as v5-fresh did.

stages.name: Walk fast
stages.reward: the real environment reward (fall −100) − (40 × lopsided + 20 × |average offset|) × share of the course covered
terms: a fall, as in the real game
as in stage 3, so the form stays while it speeds up
stages.episode: full 1600 steps, early stop on stall
stages.pass: no stage test: runs until it plateaus or 6 h; then the goal check below
stages.expect: The same alternating walk, faster and cheaper: reaches the finish with less effort and few falls, raw score ≥ 250.
stages.risk: Speed returns the skip (cheaper per unit) if the tax is too small; or more falls as it speeds up.

title: Attempt 2: balance with feet together → real steps → walk → walk fast
note: Attempt 1's balance champion stood with its feet 2.9 units apart, foot 2 always in front (the skipper's stance). Its step stage then learned to TAP its feet alternately in that split stance: ~70 alternating touchdowns, 0 front-foot changes, σ collapsed to 0.013. Attempt 2 balances with the feet together, and only counts a touchdown as a step when the foot coming down is the front foot. Stages 3 and 4 are unchanged. Stopped Wed 12:40 in stage 2: stood still with the feet together (≈1 front-foot change per episode, σ collapsed).

title: Attempt 4: training wheels. Walk with an upright support that fades out (2 → 1 → 0.5 → 0), then walk fast
note: Attempts 2 and 3 got stuck on opposite sides of the same gap: attempt 2's step stage chose to stand still with the feet together (falling while stepping costs too much), attempt 3 kept the alternating stumble and fell on all 20 tracks through the step and walk stages. Attempt 4 lets the stumbler learn to walk while an upright torque keeps it from tipping over, then fades that support out in stages, so balance is learned gradually. At support 2 the stumbler never falls and steps in place.

stages.risk: Leans on the support (lets it do the balancing), then falls when the support is reduced; or keeps stepping in place.

title: Attempt 5: polish the alternating walker (cheaper steps)
note: Attempt 4's walk-fast champion meets the goal (about 276 on the held-out tracks, no falls, feet sharing the lead), but it spends about 99 points on motor effort per run against the skipper's 75, and its search is converging (σ 0.015). Attempt 5 continues from it with effort counting 1.5 times in training, the real fall cost and the same gait tax, a small σ0 (0.05) and a larger population (64) for fine-tuning. The champion is still chosen by the real score plus the gait tax. Stopped Wed 20:30 after converging; its champion (284 held-out raw, 279.4 on the goal check, no falls) seeds attempt 7.

stages.reward: real game reward (fall −100) − 0.5 × effort − (40 × lopsided + 20 × |offset|) × share of course

(40 × lopsided + 20 × |offset|) × share of course: keeps the feet taking turns
stages.episode: 1600 steps, early stop on stall, no support (cap 10 h)
stages.pass: no stage test: runs until it plateaus; goal check on the page
stages.expect: The same alternating walk with less motor effort, so a higher real score (above the current ≈ 276 held-out).
stages.risk: Saves effort by slipping back toward a lopsided gait (the gait tax should stop that), or by slowing down.

title: Attempt 6: a wider network (64 hidden units), widened without forgetting
note: The shared leg controller has 32 hidden neurons. More capacity may allow a smoother, cheaper gait. The champion of attempt 4 is widened to 64 hidden neurons Net2Net-style: the new neurons start with zero outgoing weights, so the widened network walks exactly like the original (same 272.79 on the replay track, 1,859 parameters instead of 931), and CMA-ES then learns to use the extra capacity. Only the size changes (no extra effort weight), so it can be compared cleanly with attempt 5. Queued to start when attempt 4's last stage ends. Stopped Wed 22:30 after converging (σ 0.007); its latest champion scored 250.0 with 3 falls on the goal check.

stages.pass: no stage test: runs until it plateaus; goal check on the page
stages.expect: Uses the extra neurons for a smoother, cheaper gait: a higher real score than the 32-neuron walker.
stages.risk: Twice the parameters make the search slower; it may not beat the narrow network within the time left.

title: Attempt 7: combine the two ideas: wider network + cheaper steps
note: Attempt 5 (effort ×1.5) gave the best walker so far: 279.4 on the goal check with no falls, effort down from 99 to 84. It had converged (σ 0.011, +4.6 over 200 generations), so it was stopped at generation ~291 with its champion kept. Attempt 6 (64 neurons, no extra effort cost) is still improving slowly. Attempt 7 combines both: attempt 5's champion widened to 64 neurons, with the 1.5× effort cost. Stopped Thu 00:40. Its champion looked like 288 with no falls on 20 goal tracks, but scored 262.9 ± 62.9 with 14 falls on 100 comparison tracks.

title: Attempt 8: precision. More tracks per candidate and for choosing the champion
note: The goal check exposed the winner's curse: attempt 5's newer champion looked better on its 20 selection tracks but scored 270.6 with 2 falls on the goal tracks (its earlier one had 279.4 and no falls), and attempt 6's latest champion fell 3 times (250.0, failing the safe requirement). At this level falls are rare events, and 5 training tracks plus 20 selection tracks pick lucky walkers. Attempt 8 continues from the best walker, attempt 7's champion (284.4 on the goal check, no falls), with 10 tracks per candidate and 40 selection tracks, a small step size, the 64-neuron network, the 1.5× effort cost and the gait tax. Attempt 6 was stopped (converged).

title: Attempt 9: safety. Falls cost double in training
note: A 100-track paired check overturned the 20-track goal checks: attempt 7's champion (288 with 0 falls on 20 goal tracks) scored 262.9 ± 62.9 with 14 falls on 100 comparison tracks, attempt 8's 267.0 ± 60.2 with 12 falls; the difference between them is noise. They are faster (about 880 steps) and cheaper (effort 73) than yesterday's 263.9 ± 1.1, 0-fall walker, but trade safety for it. The goal check now uses 50 tracks (≤ 10% falls). Attempt 9 continues from attempt 7's champion with a fall costing 200 in training, 10 tracks per candidate and 40 selection tracks. Attempt 7 was stopped; attempt 8 continues.
